footprint.notes: Intel publishes no 50-state breakdown. Its April 2025 U.S. fact sheet (company-hosted PDF) gives investment figures for its four manufacturing states only (Oregon, Arizona, New Mexico, Ohio); no newer edition found (checked 2026-11-24). The live intel.com usa-chipmaking page (moved from /usa-chipmaking/home.html, which now redirects) is undated and shows slightly higher cumulative figures ($65B Oregon since 1974, $34.5B Arizona since 1979, $17.68B New Mexico since 1980) plus 2023 state GDP contributions; the dated fact sheet is kept, and the page is cited only for the site descriptions. Cumulative investment and new-project figures are different measures and must not be added. The fact sheet also lists CHIPS Act awards per state (AZ $3.94B, NM $500M, OR $1.86B, OH $1.5B); these are government funding to Intel, not Intel's footprint, and are not recorded. Nationally, the usa-chipmaking page says Intel directly employs 45k people in the U.S. (company-published); not recorded as a row because the U.S. row's source is the 10-K PP&E table. A 2021 third-party study (FY2019 data) covering AZ, CA, NM and OR exists but is far older and was not used. PP&E by country is from the FY2025 10-K (Dec 27, 2025). 10-K Properties gives only square feet: U.S. 37 million (35 owned, 2 leased) vs other countries 28 million; there are no per-state or per-country site counts, so the 10-K's key production fabs (Oregon, Arizona, Ireland, Israel) and key assembly and test sites (China, New Mexico, Vietnam, Malaysia) appear as sites. The Costa Rica assembly and test site was removed: the FY2025 10-K no longer lists it and says Intel initiated the consolidation of its Costa Rican assembly and test operations into larger existing sites in Vietnam and Malaysia. The same passage says Intel slowed construction of the Ohio fab and discontinued planned expansions in Germany and Poland.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 27, 2025 (FY2025 Form 10-K, accession 0000050863-26-000011). Capex is gross additions to PP&E, not netted against 1,577 of capital-related government incentives. Capex excludes 3,026 of PP&E additions paid to capital vendors under extended payment terms (over 90 days), which Intel reports in financing activities (1,178 in 2024); including them would raise paidOut to 60.828. Intel reports no separate intangible-purchase line. Interest and taxes paid are inside operating cash flow (US GAAP); income taxes paid now come from the income-tax note. Divestiture proceeds (6,157 net) are investing and excluded.

owners.notes: NBIM: the quote is this company's equity row in NBIM's holdings data file at June 30, 2026 ("o" = ownership %, "eq.v" = voting %, "a.e" = market value in USD, "a.n" = in NOK); NBIM also holds Intel corporate bonds, in a separate row that is not counted. CalPERS: the source is the information table of CalPERS's Form 13F for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Form 13F covers only U.S.-listed securities, and the quoted row gives issuer, class, CUSIP, value in dollars and shares. The CalPERS percentage divides its September 30, 2026 shares by the Q3 2026 10-Q cover count at October 23, 2026, which is rounded to millions, the same count used in the marketcap lens.
